_comment: Shared RFC 8785 golden vectors for src/mcp_pin/digest.py and
js/mcp-pin-check/index.js. Both languages load THIS file and assert the
same `canonical` string, so the two implementations cannot drift apart
in silence the way they did before JCS.
Keep this file ASCII-escaped. It deliberately contains a lone surrogate,
which is legal in JSON but cannot be written as raw UTF-8 -- a rewrite
with ensure_ascii=False will fail or corrupt it.
`refuses` is checked in Python only. By the time JavaScript sees a number,
JSON.parse has already collapsed it to a double, so a literal that lost
precision looks identical to one that did not. Python's arbitrary-precision
ints can still tell, so the refusal lives on the side that writes the lock.

canonical.why: a float that is integral -- the Pydantic/FastMCP bound that used to split the two sides
negative zero folds, because ECMAScript String(-0) is '0'
1e16 is above 2**53 and still exact, so it is written in full
1e20 is still inside the full-decimal window
1e-7 is the first small value in exponent notation
shortest round-tripping repr, which both languages already share
C0 control that has no short escape
non-ASCII stays raw -- JCS does not backslash-escape it
astral character stays raw as one code point
a LONE surrogate is escaped rather than crashing the encoder
array order is preserved, never sorted
BMP private-use vs astral: UTF-16 order puts the astral pair FIRST, code-point order would not
nesting, with an integral float inside

refuses.why: an integer that loses precision as a double cannot round-trip through JavaScript

digests.why: the Pydantic-shaped tool that used to report false drift in the plugin hook
a description carrying a lone surrogate
wire spellings and the omit-when-empty fields
